thread:
Samira (VP Eng): :wave: Thanks everyone — starting a quick live Q&A from today's all‑hands on engineering process (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Drop questions and we'll answer in thread.

Aisha (Product): Quick q — are we shifting to a monthly release cadence or staying with smaller weekly patches for non-critical features?

Nick (Release Manager): Short answer: mix. Major platform releases quarterly; monthly feature releases for higher-risk items; weekly patch windows for low-risk improvements and critical fixes. :+1: Canary rollouts for all pushes.

Marta (IC - QA): What exactly do we require for "quality bar" on runtime changes? e2e mandatory?

Samira (VP Eng): For runtime/routing changes: unit tests + integration tests + smoke e2e in CI are required before merge. Perf/regression test against a canonical prompt set is mandatory. We don't enforce a single coverage % for the whole repo, but critical modules should have focused coverage and tests (guideline: key modules >= 70%).

Kai (Eng Manager, Runtime): Any template for canary durations? We have too many ad‑hoc rollouts.

Nick (Release Manager): Yes — standard rollout policy (applies unless product asks for custom):
```
canary:
  - pct: 10
    dur: 24h
  - pct: 50
    dur: 12h
  - pct: 100
    dur: 2h
```
If any regression signal (error rate, latency spike, QA failure) we pause and rollback. Automation will auto‑promote if all checks pass.

Jordan (SRE Lead): Oncall changes: primary rotation = 1 week, secondary covers 2 weeks. Pager escalation: primary -> secondary after 15m if unresolved -> SRE lead after another 15m. Runbooks must be linked on each pager alert and kept up to date. :rotating_light:

Marta (IC - QA): Who owns runbook reviews?

Jordan (SRE Lead): Each runbook has an owner tag; owners must review quarterly or after any related service change. If you get a pager and the runbook is broken, escalate to oncall manager and file an incident.

Olivia (Head of Customer): For Dedicated/Enterprise customers — what SLAs are we promising? uptime + latency?

Samira (VP Eng): SLA summary: Hosted Standard: 99.9% availability. Dedicated: 99.95% availability (backed by reserved capacity). Enterprise: negotiable, with optional on‑prem/private packages. Latency SLOs are workload dependent; guidance: for small prompt short gens we target 95th ≤ 800ms, but customers can opt into premium latency tiers with reserved capacity and placement.

Aisha (Product): Freeze windows — how far before a major release?

Nick (Release Manager): Major release freeze: 7 days for features, 48 hours for infra/config changes. Exception process exists (emergency fixes handled via hotfix policy and must be signed off by Release + SRE).

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started for release/v2026.03.10

Samira (VP Eng): We'll publish an RFC summarizing these and add a checklist in the release playbook. Expect links in #docs in the next 24h. :memo:

Aisha (Product): Can someone add the checklist to the onboarding flow for new hires? That would reduce mistakes.

Samira (VP Eng): Agreed — I'll assign that to Growth Ops and DevEx. Thanks all — keep questions here and we'll update the doc.

Nick (Release Manager): TL;DR: quarterly major, monthly features, weekly patches, standard canary above, oncall = 1w primary/2w secondary, SLAs: hosted 99.9 / ded 99.95. :white_check_mark:

Marta (IC - QA): Thanks — very helpful. I'll add the regression set to CI and share the link.

Jordan (SRE Lead): Follow‑up: we'll run a simulated pager rotation drill next week — signups in #eng-sre.

Samira (VP Eng): Closing thread — will post RFC link shortly. :rocket:
